description: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the relationship between "Perplexity" and "Sparsity Rate" for two distinct categories. The horizontal axis displays the categories, labeled "Sparsity Rate," which are ordered sequentially from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%. The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "Perplexity," and utilizes a logarithmic scale ranging from below 10^1 to 10^3, with major tick marks and corresponding horizontal dashed grid lines at 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The chart features grouped bars, where each sparsity rate category contains two adjacent bars. According to the legend in the upper left corner, the blue bars positioned on the left of each group represent "Per-Output," while the orange bars on the right correspond to a category whose text label is visually obscured by a solid gray rectangle. The bar heights generally increase from left to right across the chart. At the lowest sparsity rate of 10%, both the blue and orange bars represent the shortest values, sitting just below the 10^1 mark at approximately 5 or 6. The values remain relatively stable up to 40%, after which they begin to rise more noticeably. At the highest sparsity rate of 80%, the bars reach their maximum heights, with the blue "Per-Output" bar reaching approximately 500 and the orange bar reaching nearly 10^3, at approximately 900. The groups are sorted in ascending numerical order based on the sparsity rate percentages, and there are no specific visual emphases on the bars themselves.
